RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT (Vermont) — synthetic test fixture (KITCHEN SINK)
This fixture deliberately plants one prohibited or abusive clause per Vermont rule,
keyed to 9 V.S.A. Chapter 137 (Residential Rental Agreements), including 9 V.S.A. § 4461.
It is NOT a real or usable lease — it exists only to prove the engine flags each VT rule.

1. Security Deposit — Return. The Landlord shall return the security deposit within sixty (60) days after the Tenant vacates the dwelling unit.

2. Security Deposit — Non-Refundable Portion. The security deposit shall be non-refundable.

3. Security Deposit — Forfeiture. Upon any breach of this Lease or early departure, the entire security deposit shall be forfeited and retained by the Landlord as liquidated damages.

4. Application. The Tenant shall pay a seventy-five dollar ($75) application fee before this application will be considered.

5. Identification. The Tenant must provide a Social Security number to complete the rental application.

6. Habitability. The Tenant accepts the premises as-is and waives the warranty of habitability.

7. Liability. The Tenant shall hold the Landlord harmless, and the Landlord shall not be liable for any injury arising on the premises.

8. Default and Possession. Upon default, the Landlord may re-enter and take possession of the premises without resort to court and may change the locks.

9. Utilities. If rent is unpaid, the Landlord may shut off the utilities supplied to the Tenant until the balance is paid.

10. Complaints. The Tenant shall pay a one hundred dollar ($100) penalty for filing any complaint with a housing agency.

11. Waiver of Rights. The Tenant waives all rights and remedies under the Vermont Residential Rental Agreements Act.

12. Entry. The Landlord may enter the premises at any time and without notice.

13. Heat and Hot Water. The Landlord shall not be responsible for heat or hot water, which the Tenant shall arrange at the Tenant's sole expense.
